html:
John Calvin was a French theologian who made Geneva the centre of Reformed Protestantism. Born in 1509 in Noyon, he fled France and settled in Geneva for most of the years from 1536 to his death in 1564.

His Institutes of the Christian Religion set out a strict theology, with God's sovereignty and predestination at its heart. In Geneva he built a disciplined church run by pastors and elders, which oversaw the morals of the whole city. Refugees came to Geneva from across Europe and took his model home.

Calvinism shaped the Dutch Reformed Church, the Huguenots of France, the Presbyterians of Scotland under John Knox, and the Puritans of England and New England. It fed the Dutch Revolt and later ideas of resistance to kings. His heirs in Switzerland joined with the followers of Zwingli.
